newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds were lower in late trade but off early session lows while the curve flattened as shorter-dated debt prices continued to decline.
The December confederate bond contract saw profit-taking after nearly regaining the October 9 high of 115.80 on Tuesday.
Volume was light with Conf futures volume seen at only 1,200 contracts. Traders said the downward pressure on prices resulted in part from the mark's gains against the Swiss franc.
"The move down today was due to the forex move," one trader said, adding the mark's rise to as high as 84.28 centimes today was a key reason for selling in a fairly quiet market.
Investor demand may also have been subdued ahead of the conclusion of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
U.S. producer prices for October showed a rise of 0.4 percent, and a drop of 0.3 percent excluding food and energy. The data had little lasting price impact.

Swiss power provider Electricite d'Emosson launched a 12-year 75 million Swiss franc bond, with a 4-1/4 percent coupon via UBS UIXL. The issue was the third 12-year offering by a power company this month. Engadiner Kraftwerke set a 100 million 12-year issue via SBC November 6 SBHC, and Grande Dixence set a 125 million 12-year bond via SBC November 12.
One syndicate manager said that power companies prefer to take up long-term financing which better matches their long-term investments in energy projects.
The timing for such offerings has been favourable given that yields of Swiss 10-year federal government bonds are now well below the 4.00 percent level sought by domestic institutional investors.
Such investors are likely to prefer the higher coupons on the latest 12-year offerings, the syndicate manager said.
Grande Dixence was quoted on one dealer screen yielding 4.18 percent in late trade.
Dec Comi medium-term bond down 28 at 110.15
March Euro Swiss francs down 10 at 97.80.
